title: Climate Change Discussion

script.speaker: A
script.text: Do you think climate change is the biggest problem facing our planet?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Absolutely. Rising temperatures are causing extreme weather events worldwide.

script.speaker: A
script.text: But some people argue that the economy should take priority.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's short-sighted. Without a stable climate, the economy will suffer far more.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What changes do you think individuals can make?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Reducing meat consumption, using public transport, and cutting energy waste.

script.speaker: A
script.text: But isn't it corporations that cause most pollution?

script.speaker: B
script.text: True — about seventy percent of emissions come from just one hundred companies.

script.speaker: A
script.text: So we need stronger government regulation.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Exactly. Both individual action and systemic change are necessary.

questions.stemText: What does Speaker B think about prioritizing the economy over climate?
What percentage of emissions come from 100 companies?
Rising temperatures cause extreme ___ events.
Both individual action and systemic ___ are necessary.
Match each individual action to its category.

fullScript:
A: Do you think climate change is the biggest problem facing our planet?
B: Absolutely. Rising temperatures are causing extreme weather events worldwide.
A: But some people argue that the economy should take priority.
B: That's short-sighted. Without a stable climate, the economy will suffer far more.
A: What changes do you think individuals can make?
B: Reducing meat consumption, using public transport, and cutting energy waste.
A: But isn't it corporations that cause most pollution?
B: True — about seventy percent of emissions come from just one hundred companies.
A: So we need stronger government regulation.
B: Exactly. Both individual action and systemic change are necessary.

title: Technology in Education

script.speaker: A
script.text: Technology is transforming how we teach and learn. Do you see this in your school?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Definitely. We use tablets instead of textbooks now, and lessons are often interactive.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What are the main benefits?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Students can learn at their own pace, and teachers can track progress in real-time.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What about disadvantages?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Distraction is a problem. Students sometimes use devices for social media instead of studying.

script.speaker: A
script.text: And not all students have equal access to technology.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's the digital divide. Students from lower-income families are often left behind.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How can schools address this?

script.speaker: B
script.text: By providing devices to all students and ensuring reliable internet access.

questions.stemText: What do students use instead of textbooks?
What is the 'digital divide'?
options: Gap between old and new technology

questions.stemText: Students can learn at their own ___.
Teachers can track progress in ___.
Match technology benefit or problem.

fullScript:
A: Technology is transforming how we teach and learn. Do you see this in your school?
B: Definitely. We use tablets instead of textbooks now, and lessons are often interactive.
A: What are the main benefits?
B: Students can learn at their own pace, and teachers can track progress in real-time.
A: What about disadvantages?
B: Distraction is a problem. Students sometimes use devices for social media instead of studying.
A: And not all students have equal access to technology.
B: That's the digital divide. Students from lower-income families are often left behind.
A: How can schools address this?
B: By providing devices to all students and ensuring reliable internet access.

title: Cultural Differences in Communication

script.speaker: A
script.text: Have you noticed cultural differences in the way people communicate at work?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Very much so. In some cultures, direct communication is valued. In others, it's considered rude.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Can you give an example?

script.speaker: B
script.text: In Germany, people tend to be very direct. In Japan, disagreement is often expressed indirectly.

script.speaker: A
script.text: That could cause misunderstandings in international business.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Absolutely. What's considered professional in one culture may seem aggressive or evasive in another.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How can we bridge these differences?

script.speaker: B
script.text: By developing cultural intelligence — learning about other cultures before working with them.

script.speaker: A
script.text: And being willing to adapt your communication style.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Exactly. Flexibility and empathy are key in cross-cultural communication.

questions.stemText: How do people in Germany typically communicate?
According to Speaker B, what is key in cross-cultural communication?
Developing ___ intelligence means learning about other cultures.
In Japan, disagreement is often expressed ___.
Match country to communication style.

fullScript:
A: Have you noticed cultural differences in the way people communicate at work?
B: Very much so. In some cultures, direct communication is valued. In others, it's considered rude.
A: Can you give an example?
B: In Germany, people tend to be very direct. In Japan, disagreement is often expressed indirectly.
A: That could cause misunderstandings in international business.
B: Absolutely. What's considered professional in one culture may seem aggressive or evasive in another.
A: How can we bridge these differences?
B: By developing cultural intelligence — learning about other cultures before working with them.
A: And being willing to adapt your communication style.
B: Exactly. Flexibility and empathy are key in cross-cultural communication.

title: Career Planning

script.speaker: A
script.text: I'm trying to decide what career to pursue after graduation. Any advice?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Think about what skills you enjoy using and what problems you want to solve.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I love writing and research. But I also enjoy working with people.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's a good combination. Journalism, communications, or HR could suit you.

script.speaker: A
script.text: I've heard the job market is very competitive now.

script.speaker: B
script.text: It is, but employers value soft skills — communication, adaptability, teamwork.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Should I do an internship before applying for jobs?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Absolutely. Experience is often more valuable than a degree on your CV.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What about networking?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Essential. Many jobs are filled through personal connections, not job advertisements.

questions.stemText: What skills does Speaker A enjoy using?
According to Speaker B, what do employers value?
Many jobs are filled through ___ connections.
Experience is often more valuable than a ___ on your CV.
Match soft skill to its meaning.

fullScript:
A: I'm trying to decide what career to pursue after graduation. Any advice?
B: Think about what skills you enjoy using and what problems you want to solve.
A: I love writing and research. But I also enjoy working with people.
B: That's a good combination. Journalism, communications, or HR could suit you.
A: I've heard the job market is very competitive now.
B: It is, but employers value soft skills — communication, adaptability, teamwork.
A: Should I do an internship before applying for jobs?
B: Absolutely. Experience is often more valuable than a degree on your CV.
A: What about networking?
B: Essential. Many jobs are filled through personal connections, not job advertisements.

title: Social Media and Society

script.speaker: A
script.text: Social media has changed how we communicate. Is that a positive or negative change?

script.speaker: B
script.text: It's both. Social media connects people globally but also spreads misinformation rapidly.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Mental health is a big concern. Studies show it increases anxiety in young people.

script.speaker: B
script.text: Particularly when users compare themselves to unrealistic images online.

script.speaker: A
script.text: But it also gives a voice to people who were previously unheard.

script.speaker: B
script.text: True. Social movements like climate activism have been amplified through social media.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What about privacy? Companies collect enormous amounts of personal data.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's a serious issue. Most users don't realize how their data is being used.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What's the solution?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Better regulation and digital literacy education from an early age.

questions.stemText: What negative mental health effect is mentioned?
What solution does Speaker B propose?
Social media spreads misinformation ___.
Social movements like climate activism have been ___ through social media.
Match social media impact to type.

fullScript:
A: Social media has changed how we communicate. Is that a positive or negative change?
B: It's both. Social media connects people globally but also spreads misinformation rapidly.
A: Mental health is a big concern. Studies show it increases anxiety in young people.
B: Particularly when users compare themselves to unrealistic images online.
A: But it also gives a voice to people who were previously unheard.
B: True. Social movements like climate activism have been amplified through social media.
A: What about privacy? Companies collect enormous amounts of personal data.
B: That's a serious issue. Most users don't realize how their data is being used.
A: What's the solution?
B: Better regulation and digital literacy education from an early age.

title: Urban vs Rural Living

script.speaker: A
script.text: Would you prefer to live in a city or the countryside?

script.speaker: B
script.text: I'd choose the city for the career opportunities and cultural life.

script.speaker: A
script.text: But cities are increasingly stressful and expensive.

script.speaker: B
script.text: That's true. Many young professionals are moving to mid-sized cities instead.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Rural areas offer a better quality of life in many ways.

script.speaker: B
script.text: If you can work remotely. The pandemic made that more possible for many people.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Do you think cities are becoming less desirable?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Some are, due to high housing costs and pollution. But they still attract talent.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What would be your ideal living situation?

script.speaker: B
script.text: A village within commuting distance of a city — best of both worlds.

questions.stemText: Why does Speaker B prefer the city?
What is Speaker B's ideal living situation?
Many young professionals are moving to ___ cities.
Working ___ made rural living more possible.
Match advantage to location.

fullScript:

B: I'd choose the city for the career opportunities and cultural life.

B: That's true. Many young professionals are moving to mid-sized cities instead.
A: Rural areas offer a better quality of life in many ways.
B: If you can work remotely. The pandemic made that more possible for many people.
A: Do you think cities are becoming less desirable?
B: Some are, due to high housing costs and pollution. But they still attract talent.
A: What would be your ideal living situation?
B: A village within commuting distance of a city — best of both worlds.

title: Travel and Cultural Exchange

script.speaker: A
script.text: Have you ever lived abroad?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, I spent a year in Argentina teaching English. It was life-changing.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What was the most challenging part?

script.speaker: B
script.text: The language barrier at first, and adjusting to a completely different daily routine.

script.speaker: A
script.text: And what did you gain from the experience?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Fluency in Spanish, a completely new perspective, and lifelong friendships.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Do you think everyone should experience living abroad?

script.speaker: B
script.text: If possible, yes. It breaks down stereotypes and develops empathy.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What advice would you give someone planning to move abroad?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Learn the language before you go and embrace discomfort — that's where growth happens.

questions.stemText: Where did Speaker B live abroad?
What did Speaker B gain from the experience?
options: Fluency in Spanish and new friendships
questions.answer: Fluency in Spanish and new friendships

questions.stemText: Speaker B spent ___ year abroad teaching English.
Living abroad breaks down ___ and develops empathy.
Match challenge to benefit of living abroad.

title: Volunteering and Community Service

script.speaker: A
script.text: I'm thinking about doing some volunteer work. Have you done any?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Yes, I volunteered at a food bank last year. It was very rewarding.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What did you do there?

script.speaker: B
script.text: We sorted and packed food donations for families in need. It was physically demanding but fulfilling.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How often did you volunteer?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Every Saturday for six months. About four hours each time.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Did it affect your career?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Positively. It showed employers I have initiative and care about my community.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What skills did you develop?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Teamwork, time management, and empathy for people in difficult situations.

title: Language Learning Strategies

script.speaker: A
script.text: What's the best way to learn a foreign language quickly?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Immersion is most effective. Surround yourself with the language as much as possible.

script.speaker: A
script.text: Is that possible without living abroad?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Absolutely. Change your phone language, watch films without subtitles, and find language exchange partners.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What about apps like language learning platforms?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Useful for vocabulary and grammar, but they can't replace real conversation practice.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How important is making mistakes?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Crucial. Fear of making mistakes is the biggest barrier for adult learners.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How long does it take to become fluent?

script.speaker: B
script.text: It depends on the language and your native tongue. A thousand hours of study is a common estimate.

questions.stemText: What does Speaker B say is most effective for language learning?
What is the biggest barrier for adult learners?
A common estimate for fluency is ___ hours of study.
Language apps can't replace real ___ practice.
Match immersion strategy to activity.

fullScript:
A: What's the best way to learn a foreign language quickly?
B: Immersion is most effective. Surround yourself with the language as much as possible.
A: Is that possible without living abroad?
B: Absolutely. Change your phone language, watch films without subtitles, and find language exchange partners.
A: What about apps like language learning platforms?
B: Useful for vocabulary and grammar, but they can't replace real conversation practice.
A: How important is making mistakes?
B: Crucial. Fear of making mistakes is the biggest barrier for adult learners.
A: How long does it take to become fluent?
B: It depends on the language and your native tongue. A thousand hours of study is a common estimate.

title: Health Care Systems

script.speaker: A
script.text: How does the healthcare system work in your country?

script.speaker: B
script.text: We have a universal system — everyone is covered regardless of income.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How is it funded?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Through taxes. We pay more in tax but don't pay medical bills directly.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What are the main advantages?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Equality of access. Your health shouldn't depend on your wealth.

script.speaker: A
script.text: What are the challenges?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Long waiting times and an aging population placing more demands on the system.

script.speaker: A
script.text: How does it compare to private healthcare?

script.speaker: B
script.text: Private is faster but expensive and inaccessible for low-income people.

What is a challenge of universal healthcare?

Match healthcare type to characteristic.

B: Long waiting times and an aging population placing more demands on the system.

B: Private is faster but expensive and inaccessible for low-income people.
